entries.notes: Audit: the source reads 'A map is not the territory it represents, but, if correct, it has a similar structure to the territory, which accounts for its usefulness.' The manuscript carries the standard compressed form. Recorded during the census as a SOURCE RESTORATION OPPORTUNITY - the fuller sentence says more than the compression.

entries.actual_author: two halves, two origins, roughly eleven centuries apart
entries.notes: Audit: COMPOSITE ATTRIBUTION - third confirmed instance - and also SOURCE-FORM MISCLASSIFICATION. 'As above, so below' is a popular modern paraphrase of the Emerald Tablet's second verse; the other half has a separate and much later origin. THE BOOK ALSO CARRIES THE ACCURATE EMERALD TABLET FORM IN CH9 - ancestor and composite descendant, one chapter apart.

entries.match: Alchemy is a kind of philosophy
entries.notes: Audit: quote-site attestation only; no primary source. Duchamp's alchemical interests ARE scholarly-documented (Moffitt, Alchemist of the Avant-Garde, SUNY) but that supports the THEME, not the sentence. Recorded as the INVERSE of the Sai Baba case: there a documented framework initially looked contradicted and turned out compatible; here the documented preoccupation makes the sentence PLAUSIBLE, which is exactly why it must not be treated as verified. Thematic fit is not provenance, in either direction.

entries.match: What is above is like what is below
entries.notes: FAMILY ROLE: ancestor. The accurate Emerald Tablet form. Its composite descendant in Ch10 fuses it with a much later half. A family is not always a set of duplicates - it can be a lineage.
